# Unicode case-folding provenance

The reference-label normalizer uses **Unicode 17.0.0 default full case folding**.
The retained source is unmodified Unicode Character Database data:

- [CaseFolding.txt](https://www.unicode.org/Public/17.0.0/ucd/CaseFolding.txt),
  dated 2025-07-30; SHA-256
  `ff8d8fefbf123574205085d6714c36149eb946d717a0c585c27f0f4ef58c4183`.
- [Unicode License v3](https://www.unicode.org/license.txt), retained in
  `LICENSE.txt`; SHA-256
  `e7a93b009565cfce55919a381437ac4db883e9da2126fa28b91d12732bc53d96`.

The generated `internal/parser/casefold_table.go` derives C and F mappings only,
excluding simple-only S and Turkic T mappings as directed by the source's full
default folding rules. Unlisted scalars map to themselves. No normalization form,
locale mapping, entity decoding or visible-label rewriting is implied. The
matching operation separately handles the CommonMark label whitespace rule.
Unicode's data license applies to the retained data and derived table; its notice
is retained alongside the source. Runtime code uses only the Go standard library.

From the repository root, with Python 3.9+ and gofmt installed:

```sh
python3 -B tools/unicode_casefold.py
python3 -B tools/unicode_casefold.py --check
go test ./internal/parser -run 'Reference|FullCaseFold'
```

Generation and checking work offline, use this retained source rather than the
host Unicode database, verify its pinned SHA-256, and resolve paths from the
script. `--check` does not write files. CI checks exact regenerated bytes; Go tests
compare every full default mapping against the retained source and distinguish
the special Turkic mapping. Updating this Unicode version requires a reviewed
data/provenance/table change rather than following an ambient runtime upgrade.
